result.title: Learning to Act with World Models by Valuing What Comes Next
result.summary: A sparse terminal reward tells an agent little about its steps. Much of the missing information is implicit in the environment's dynamics, because each state transition can change the conditions for success long before the reward arrives. A world model trained on real transitions can learn to predict what each action changes, but a predicted observation does not by itself show whether success has become more likely. With a binary terminal reward, PPO's critic makes this judgment by estimating the current policy's probability of success, but only for states the agent reaches. Our method, WM-PPO, elegantly brings the two together. For each action the policy samples, executed or not, the world model predicts the next observation and the critic values the predicted successor. In the policy channel, comparisons among these values give the policy auxiliary advantages; in the value channel, their mean gives the critic an auxiliary target. A shared gate weights both channels according to how reliably comparisons with similar margins predicted real outcomes earlier in training. The policy, critic and world model all learn from the agent's own interaction, with no teacher or privileged information, and only the policy is used at inference. With a comparable number of real environment steps, WM-PPO raises success from PPO's 63.5% to 87.5% on ALFWorld and from 39.3% to 52.9% on ScienceWorld. It matches the strongest PPO refinements we tested on ALFWorld and exceeds the best of them by 6.5 points on ScienceWorld. The trained policy more often completes prerequisite steps before placing an object or committing to an answer.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 WM-PPO，用世界模型对环境做一步预测，再由 critic 对预测出的后继状态估值，把价值比较作为策略的辅助优势、把价值均值作为 critic 的辅助目标，并用一个共享门控按历史预测可靠性加权。
AI.relevance_reason: 纯文本具身任务，不含视觉 latent，但「对想象后继状态估值以分配中间步贡献、按可靠性门控辅助信号」可能为 LVR 中推理步贡献分配与何时采信预测状态提供可核查的方法线索。
